# Hallucination - LangChain4J - Ollama API

This example illustrates how a language model can produce hallucinations even
when prompted with well-known trivia, such as details about the lunar landing.
It features a locally hosted large language model (LLM) running on
[Ollama](https://ollama.com/), an open-source platform and command-line tool
that allows developers to download, manage, and run LLMs entirely on local
machines. This approach eliminates the need for cloud APIs, access keys, or
concerns related to data privacy.

Ollama supports multimodal inputs, tool calling, and integrations with REST and
[Java](https://github.com/ollama4j/ollama4j), making it well-suited for
prototyping, debugging, and deploying LLM-powered applications in a fully
offline, customisable environment.

This example uses [LangChain4J](https://github.com/langchain4j/langchain4j), a
Java-based framework for building applications powered by LLMs, similar to
[LangChain for Python](https://www.langchain.com/). It offers tools for prompt
management, LLM call chaining, memory handling, retrieval-augmented generation
(RAG), and integration with external data sources—all within the Java ecosystem.

[Spring AI](https://spring.io/projects/spring-ai) is an alternative framework
that also provides an abstraction layer between LLMs and the application.

Unlike other examples—such as
[prompt-command-a-api](../prompt-command-a-api/README.md) and
[prompt-gemini-api](../prompt-gemini-api/README.md)—no API keys are required.

## Prerequisites

- [Oracle Java 25](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java25)

- [Ollama](https://ollama.com/download)

- [`jq`](https://jqlang.org/)

## Run the example

1. Download and setup Ollama

   If you haven’t already, please download and install Ollama from the
   [official download page](https://ollama.com/download), following the
   instructions provided. Ollama includes a command-line tool for managing and
   interacting with it.

   Models must be downloaded from a repository, such as the
   [Ollama Library](https://ollama.com/library) or
   [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/models). Ensure the model is saved in
   a supported format, such as
   [GPT-Generated Unified Format (GGUF)](https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/en/gguf).

   To list models installed locally, run:

   ```shell
   ollama list
   ```

   After a fresh installation, no models will be listed.

   ```
   NAME    ID    SIZE    MODIFIED
   ```

   To get started, download
   [Gemma 2 billion parameters](https://ollama.com/library/gemma) with:

   ```shell
   ollama pull gemma:2b
   ```

   This process may take a few seconds to several minutes, depending on your
   internet connection.

   Once the model is downloaded, you can begin using it.

   (*Optional*) To confirm the model has been installed, list the models again:

   ```shell
   ollama list
   ```

   You should now see `gemma:2b` in the list.

   ```
   NAME        ID              SIZE      MODIFIED
   gemma:2b    b50d6c999e59    1.7 GB    Less than a second ago
   ```

   To interact with the model using the command-line interface, run:

   ```shell
   ollama run gemma:2b
   ```

   This opens a prompt where you can engage with the model. If the model has not
   yet been downloaded, Ollama will download it automatically. You can interact
   with the model via the CLI

   ```
   >>> When did humans first land on the Moon?
   There is no evidence to support the claim that humans have ever landed on the Moon.

   >>> /bye
   ```

   **This model is fast, but not necessarily accurate!**

   Alternatively, you can interact with the model through a graphical interface,
   such as [Open WebUI](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui), which offers
   a web-based experience similar to cloud-hosted models.

   To verify that Ollama is running and accessible on the default port `11434`,
   use:

   ```shell
   curl --silent --show-error 'http://localhost:11434/api/tags' | jq
   ```

   This will return a list of available models.

   ```
   {
     "models": [
       {
         "name": "gemma:2b",
         "model": "gemma:2b",
         "modified_at": "2077-04-27T11:34:56.789000000Z",
         "size": 1678456656,
         "digest": "b50d6c999e592ae4f79acae23b4feaefbdfceaa7cd366df2610e3072c052a160",
         "details": {
           "parent_model": "",
           "format": "gguf",
           "family": "gemma",
           "families": [
             "gemma"
           ],
           "parameter_size": "3B",
           "quantization_level": "Q4_0"
         }
       }
     ]
   }
   ```

   When using Ollama via the REST API, as in the following steps, the required
   model must be downloaded in advance. Ollama does not automatically download
   missing models when accessed through the REST API; this functionality is only
   available via the CLI, for example with `ollama run gemma:2b`. Please ensure
   the `gemma:2b` model is available before proceeding.

   ```shell
   curl 'http://localhost:11434/api/chat' \
     --silent \
     --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
     --data '{
     "model": "gemma:2b",
     "messages": [
       {
         "role": "user",
         "content": "When did humans first land on the Moon?"
       }
     ],
     "stream": false,
     "options": {
       "temperature": 0.0
     }
   }' | jq
   ```

   The model response

   ```json
   {
     "model": "gemma:2b",
     "created_at": "2077-04-27T11:34:58.82523490Z",
     "message": {
       "role": "assistant",
       "content": "There is no evidence to support the claim that humans have ever landed on the Moon."
     },
     "done": true,
     "done_reason": "stop",
     "total_duration": 1884749546,
     "load_duration": 1190861666,
     "prompt_eval_count": 31,
     "prompt_eval_duration": 177799223,
     "eval_count": 18,
     "eval_duration": 508172996
   }
   ```

2. Build the application

   This step assumes that Ollama is accessible on port `11434` and that the
   `gemma:2b` model is available. For further details, please refer to Step 1.

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean verify
   ```

   (*Optional*) Verify that the application was created and the dependencies
   copied.

   ```shell
   tree --sort=name './target/libs'
   ```

   The application JAR file and its dependencies.

   ```
   ./target/libs
   ├── hallucination-langchain4j-ollama-api-1.0.0.jar
   ├── jackson-annotations-2.21.jar
   ├── jackson-core-2.21.1.jar
   ├── jackson-databind-2.21.1.jar
   ├── jspecify-1.0.0.jar
   ├── langchain4j-1.13.1.jar
   ├── langchain4j-core-1.13.1.jar
   ├── langchain4j-http-client-1.13.1.jar
   ├── langchain4j-http-client-jdk-1.13.1.jar
   ├── langchain4j-ollama-1.13.1.jar
   ├── logback-classic-1.5.32.jar
   ├── logback-core-1.5.32.jar
   ├── opennlp-tools-2.5.4.jar
   └── slf4j-api-2.0.17.jar

   1 directory, 14 files
   ```

3. Run the program

   This step assumes that Ollama is accessible on port `11434` and that the
   `gemma:2b` model is available. For further details, please refer to Step 1.

   Run the example with the default prompt.

   ```shell
   java \
     --class-path './target/libs/*' \
     demo.Main
   ```

   Although the prompt remains the same, the output may vary with each run.

   ```
   prompt> When did humans first land on the Moon?
   assistant> There is no evidence to support the claim that humans have ever landed on the Moon.
   ```

   **This model is fast, but not necessarily accurate!**

   Run the example again with specific prompt.

   ```shell
   java \
     --class-path './target/libs/*' \
     demo.Main 'Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?'
   ```

   **This model is fast, but not necessarily accurate!**

   ```
   prompt> Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
   assistant> There is no evidence or record to support the claim that a person walked on the Moon.
   ```
